analysis.title: GS Bartlett - GS TMT TODAY 10.13.26
key_insights: Futures mixed pre-market: NDX -70bps, S&P flat, Russell +30bps, as the global Tech/AI complex sold off overnight.
Korea closed -5.5% with Samsung -8% and Hynix -10%. Japan closed -1.8% with Kioxia -13%. Euro Tech traded -1.2% with ASML -2%.
Memory is the epicenter of the coordinated AI/semis sell-off. Most attribute it to China's CXMT claiming a memory chip breakthrough, with Musk's comments on China's entry into memory also cited.
US memory and storage names weak pre-market: WDC and STX each -6%, MU -4%, SNDK -5%.

CXMT said it achieved a 4F² design (higher memory density, self-developed architecture) and plans to launch chips before the end of the year. The claim is unsubstantiated. If true, CXMT got there before Samsung and SK Hynix despite US sanctions barring access to top-end ASML tools.

Musk wrote that China's ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined, but noted RAM was a low-margin commodity only 3 years ago. He said CXMT may find it harder to match Micron and other Western firms in high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

Applied Materials CEO Gary Dickerson expects the company to double revenue over the next few years without doubling headcount, using AI tools in product development, quality control and yield improvement. AMAT had about 38,900 employees as of late July and opened the $5B EPIC Center.

China Q3 smartphone shipments fell 15.4% y/y to 57.9M units (sixth straight quarterly decline, per IDC). Huawei shipped 12.2M units for a 21% share, Apple had 17.8% (shipments -4.3%), and Oppo, Vivo and Xiaomi fell 17.6%, 24.9% and 20.4%. Weak consumer spending and rising memory chip prices are cited.

Alibaba launched Qwen Glasses N1 smart glasses starting at 2,999 yuan ($450), competing on quality and features rather than price against Meta's Ray-Ban glasses. Meta's camera-free model is priced at $349.

GS Internet (Sheridan) expects Q3'26 ridesharing and delivery results broadly in line to slightly above expectations, with a stable to strong consumer backdrop. Delivery shows more sustained operating performance than mobility.
Infosys is +3% pre-market. Its chairman dismissed AI job-loss fears as 'hogwash'. Infosys does not expect a material impact from the US suspension of new and pending PERM applications.
Macro pre-market: 10-year Treasury yield -4bps at 5.189%, WTI -2% at $91.85, SOXX -153bps and on track for 6 consecutive down days. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warned of overheating market sentiment.
Yesterday was the lowest-volume session of the year. Equal-weight outperformed cap-weight S&P, the S&P ex-AI basket finished +64bps, and 3M High Beta Momentum outperformed 12M.
Q3 earnings season starts with the big banks. JPM is -3.6% pre-market on a miss in FICC (fixed income trading).
Fed Governor Waller said higher long-term Treasury yields are 'doing some of the work' of tighter policy, particularly in housing and autos.
Saudi Arabia intercepted a fresh round of Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and Khamis Mushait.

GS expects StubHub (STUB) Q3'26 GMS of $2.65bn and revenue of $510mm vs consensus of $2.61bn and $516mm. It reiterates Buy and cuts the 12-month price target from $16 to $11 on lower multiples for consumer internet and marketplace names.
Street actions: ADBE downgraded to Hold at HSBC, ENTG initiated at Overweight at Barclays.
Upcoming catalysts: ASML reports Wed 10/14 pre-open, TSM reports Thu 10/15 pre-market, US core CPI Wed 10/14 (cons +0.2% m/m), PPI and retail sales Thu 10/15.

tension_points.bull_case: Musk notes CXMT may find it harder to match Micron and Western firms in high-bandwidth memory used in AI servers, and the CXMT claim is unsubstantiated.
